title: Since 0.17.2 "error: incomplete metadata for C:: multiple errors occurred: [get named security info failed with:"
body:
Output of `restic version`
--------------------------

0.17.2

What backend/service did you use to store the repository?
---------------------------------------------------------

Windows
Backup to another local drive and S3-compatible like MinIO and Wasabi

Problem description / Steps to reproduce
----------------------------------------

It seems that the error depands von VSS (Volume Shadow Copy Service).

command line:

`restic --limit-upload 1220 --verbose --use-fs-snapshot --compression=max backup C:\Hyper-V\SRV02`

Expected behavior
-----------------

No error.

Actual behavior
---------------

The output/llog shows this:

Log (the Windows-error is in german):

```
open repository
using parent snapshot 2c9cacd3
load index files
start scan on [C:\Hyper-V\SRV02]
start backup on [C:\Hyper-V\SRV02]
creating VSS snapshot for [c:]
successfully created snapshot for [c:]
error: incomplete metadata for C:: multiple errors occurred: [get named security info failed with: Zugriff verweigert; get EA failed while opening file handle for path \?\GLOBALROOT\Device\HarddiskVolumeShadowCopy52, with: Der Prozess kann nicht auf die Datei zugreifen, da sie von einem anderen Prozess verwendet wird.
scan finished in 6.700s: 13 files, 145.731 GiB

Files: 0 new, 4 changed, 9 unmodified
Dirs: 0 new, 6 changed, 9 unmodified
Data Blobs: 19809 new
Tree Blobs: 6 new
Added to the repository: 14.071 GiB (6.083 GiB stored)

processed 13 files, 145.731 GiB in 1:27:37
snapshot 1ee4fc7e saved
Warning: at least one source file could not be read
```

Do you have any idea what may have caused this?
-----------------------------------------------

I had no problems with 0.17.1.

Did restic help you today? Did it make you happy in any way?
------------------------------------------------------------

I'm using restic since 2021. It works great and stable.
Great job, Keep it up!

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: This is a result of https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/5097 , which fixed how metadata is read for VSS snapshots. We'll probably need some additional exception to skip metadata retrieval for `HarddiskVolumeShadowCopyXX` paths.

This error happens since version 0.17.0 (i made tests with versions 0.17.0, 0.17.1 and 0.17.2)

Version 0.17.0 was different error:

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
The error should be fixed by https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/5110 .

Please give it a try to make sure I didn't miss anything. To build the PR, download the go compiler from https://go.dev/dl/, download the code from the PR and build restic using `go build ./cmd/restic`.

Different Windows versions apparently return different sets of errors. The initial message in this issue contains both security descriptor and extended attribute errors (likely Windows 10 as I'm seeing the exact same errors). Whereas the second error sample, only reports extended attribute errors.

There will be a separate fix for the master branch. That branch is apparently affected by an additional bug that completely breaks the VSS feature.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: I've reworked the implementation of #5110 such that it works the same way as #5112. Apparently it makes a difference whether \\?\GLOBALROOT\Device\HarddiskVolumeShadowCopyXX or \\?\GLOBALROOT\Device\HarddiskVolumeShadowCopyXX\ (note the trailing backslash) is used. Only the latter can be properly used for file operations.

comments.body:
Thanks for testing.

> restic 0.17.2-dev (v0.9.5-4394-g1f0f6ad63)

@participant5 Based on the version number that commit is from ~~the `patch-release` branch~~ `master` branch but not the `fix-vss-root-volume-patch` branch.

> Fatal: unable to save snapshot: GetFileInformationByHandle \\?\GLOBALROOT\Device\HarddiskVolumeShadowCopy26: Incorrect function.

~~The above commit won't trigger that error. In fact,~~ that exact error can **only** be triggered by the `master` branch. It cannot be triggered by `fix-vss-root-volume-patch`. The `fix-vss-root-volume-patch` branch temporarily had a state that could trigger a related error, but that is fixed now.

Please double check that you're at the right commit.

[Edit]Commit `1f0f6ad63` belongs to the `master` branch not `patch-release`.[/Edit]
